KIO2.description: KIO2 performs analysis of failing Python programs to localize faults and diagnose their causes using execution traces. It records runtime behavior, identifies statements and variable values associated with failures, and provides evidence-based findings to support debugging and code repair. It also supports replaying recorded executions and aligning traces to compare different program runs.

KIO3.description: KIO3 transforms natural-language software descriptions into structured software engineering requirements. It generates user stories and acceptance criteria, evaluates the quality of user stories, and derives functional and performance-related non-functional requirements. It also supports wireframe generation.

KIO4.description: KIO4 transforms structured functional, non-functional requirements and constraints into a candidate software architecture. It returns a machine-readable architecture description with requirement traceability, diagrams and validation/review reports. It also supports refinement of an existing architecture, targeted repairs based on selected review findings and independent architecture review.

KIO5.description: KIO5 provides synthetic data generation capabilities through several generators. It provides a generation capability which calls the most relevant generator based on the use-case and an evaluation capability which assesses the quality of the synthetic data generated based on general properties and domain-specific constraints.

KIO6.description: KIO6 generates preparation plans, orchestrates them and validates the preparation quality through data-centric and model-centric evaluations. It provides two pipelines: one end-to-end pipeline which combines exploratory data analysis, automated data preparation and data validation; and a standalone validation pipeline which only considers the data-centric and model-centric validation of the given data.

KIO7.description: KIO7 provides code generation, refinement and code-quality testing through its code-generation module. It generates code from structured requirements and architecture descriptions, revises existing code using task instructions and findings from testing, debugging or other workflow assessments, and checks code quality.

KIO8.description: KIO8 assists the compilation process of a codebase for deployment on FPGAs. It provides capabilities to configure the Vitis HLS environment used for compilation. It also assesses report metrics obtained after compilation in the user environment, verifying whether user constraints are fulfilled. If gaps are detected, a capability enables modification of a previously generated Vitis configuration. Lastly, as AI models must also be deployed into FPGAs, KIO8 installs tools such as Conifer and Microsoft Brainsmith to generate hardware representations of AI models.

KIO9.description: KIO9 provides design-by-contract compliance for software artefacts: users register a compliance contract of rules drawn from GDPR, the EU AI Act and the EU Data Act, and an LLM-based compliance agent reviews source code and text such as medical reports against it, returning traceable findings with article references, locations and remediation, while a blockchain layer registers artefact hashes and verifies their integrity.

KIO10.description: KIO10 applies model-driven software engineering (MDSE) and TinyML to develop energy-efficient battery remaining useful life (RUL) models for microcontrollers. It generates a validated platform-independent model (PIM) of the RUL task and, through versioned rule-based transformation, a platform-specific model (PSM) for each eligible model-target pair. It trains or imports candidate models and compresses them through quantisation and pruning. It estimates energy per inference and searches model-target pairs to minimise energy, RUL error, deployment size and latency, returning the Pareto frontier for human selection. It also calibrates its energy estimates with imported physical board measurements and exports model artefacts and handoff contracts for KIO7 and KIO8.

KIO11.description: KIO11 generates and runs test campaigns on generated software using automated testing techniques, including fuzzing, symbolic execution and AI agents that interact with large language models (LLMs). It generates a test report containing all executed branches and instructions, test cases, detected crashes and anomalies, executable test harnesses, a summary of the test campaign and detailed logs, as well as suggestions for code improvement. A test campaign may include unit tests, integration tests and performance tests.

KIO12.description: KIO12 provides AI-based cybersecurity across the software lifecycle: locally hosted fine-tuned LLMs review source code for vulnerabilities and propose remediated code, a runtime guard checks workflow inputs and outputs against security obligations, and an ML-based NIDS detects network-level intrusions, with all results returned as structured, machine-readable reports.
